newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul won closes up on expected rise in dlr inflow.
newsitem.headline: Seoul won closes up on expected rise in dlr inflow.

text.p: The South Korean won closed higher against the dollar on Thursday due to increased dollar selling on expectations of rising dollar inflows, dealers said.
Dollar selling increased after the finance ministry said it would allow more issuances of beneficiary certificates for foreign investment in local stocks and bonds.
Dealers said traders were already reluctant to carry long dollar positions ahead of the May 1 expansion of the foreign shareholding limit to 23 percent from the current 20 percent.
The won closed at 892.50, up from Wednesday's 894.30. It opened at 894.50 and moved in a 891.60-895.50 range.
